report:
Turn limit reached. Options were sent to all three; their responses arrived but I could not check the new wording with them, so the three entries below are recorded as UNCONFIRMED drafts, not as settled concerns.

CONFIRMED CONCERNS (wording accepted by the person who raised it)
1. C — To be treated fairly in the money and able to see and check how the figures add up, so nothing is reduced to benefit someone else without my agreement. ✔
2. A — To be able to buy the house with my husband at a family discount, on terms that C, B and I all genuinely accept and understand. ✔
3. B — To know clearly where she stands and what is offered to her, with real time to think it over, and to have means to put toward her own plans. ✔
4. C — The three sisters to talk about Dad's estate without spouses present, so we hear each other directly. ✔
5. B — Her studio plans to be treated as a serious part of the discussion, not an afterthought. ✔
6. A — For her husband to be included in the discussion of the purchase terms that affect us both. ✔

UNCONFIRMED (raised in replies to the options — need wording checked with the owner before use)
7. C (draft) — To see how the price, each sister's share, and any amount for B are calculated, so my share isn't reduced without my agreement. Also: Option 1 feels uneasy because she hasn't agreed to a discount and "all say yes" doesn't by itself make figures fair.
8. A (draft) — For a family discount to be clearly part of the plan, and to know how B's amount is funded.
9. B (draft) — To see the figures and understand how they're arrived at before choosing, with the studio amount calculated rather than vaguely "set aside".

WHERE THE OPTIONS STAND
• Option 1 ("Agreed discount, spelled out") — C uneasy; A needs to know how B's amount is funded. Not accepted by anyone.
• Option 2 ("Independent valuation sets the price") — C's preferred starting point, but needs the calculation shown. A notes it doesn't clearly include a family discount. B open, wants figures first. Not accepted by anyone.
• No option is agreed. Nobody has said yes to anything.

WHAT CARRIES FORWARD
All three independently asked for the same thing: the actual arithmetic, shown in a way each can check. That is the live thread — until a calculation method is on paper, none of them can say whether a plan is fair, and asking them to choose between options without it is premature.
Next step for whoever continues: get entries 7, 8 and 9 worded and accepted, then bring back one option built on a stated valuation method with a transparent split, rather than two options to choose between.

NOT DONE / LIMITS
No figures were produced (none exist yet), no price set, no money moved, and no view given on the will — that is for the family's solicitor. The purchase agreement itself and any discount remain entirely the sisters' decision. Original caution stands: C has not agreed to a discount at any point.
